473.t: Cab offers loans to buy a horn through road manager Mr. Wright
473.s: Cab afterwards behaved perfectly and offered advances to buy an instrument interest-free, repaid weekly; Jones used it for an Olds trumpet and learned other leaders refused such loans.
473.ch: Cab Calloway's band, features and small groups
473.q: But we -- after that he'd ask me, he'd say, "Now, if you want to buy a horn, don't go to no bank and get the money." He says, "If you want to buy a horn I'll let you have the money to pay down on it and you can pay it back like you want to. You can give it back to Mr. Wright, you know, as you want…

473.t: Cab's pay and paid August and Christmas vacations
473.s: Cab paid better than others and gave four weeks off in August and two at Christmas with full pay and fare, something Jones had never known.
473.q: But I know one thing he did better. He would give you the full month of August off with full pay, for your vacation, every year, four weeks salary. But you was working from one year to the other, you know, right straight through, January to December, but he would give you four weeks off in August…

473.t: Cab directs every solo: the high F lesson on "Geechee Joe"
473.s: At a morning Strand Theater show Jones skipped his usual high F ending and Cab, who directs each soloist's ending with his stick, scolded him; he says late nights are no excuse.
473.q: you know, and he's just hollering for more. Stuff's hollering for more. And over there you played just what you were supposed to play, you know, with Cab. So I said, well, that's it. I'm not going to kill myself with the whiskey over there with Stuff, drinking every night, you know. And had had a…

473.t: Cab's valets and the ammonia stick after late nights
473.s: Cab had three valets; after a night out his valet Rudolph put him in a cold shower and held ammonia under his nose in the wings during "Minnie the Moocher".
473.q: But you see, what he had, see we had three valets. Now, one was just to take care of him, see, and this valet, see, he'd be hanging, drunk, and that valet, Rudolph, he'd take him in there and put him in the shower, cold shower, And then, he'd go out there and shake his head on "Minnie the Moocher"…

473.t: Cab's strict discipline: no drinking or pot, and firing the clique
473.s: Cab sniffed dressing rooms for marijuana because he feared headlines linking him to his men's habits, fired offenders with two weeks' pay and fare home, and said he would fire any clique.
473.q: Because you've got the dressing rooms back there and Cab's always passing by, and smelling, to see if he could smell any pot coming out of anyplace. And if he -- I'll tell you one thing he did. They call this hard, but I think he was right. I asked him about it once. I said, 'How come you're so…

473.t: Rotating features and Cab dropping Cozy Cole's drum number
473.s: Features were rotated every six months and Cab cut shows by telling Cozy only on stage that his drum number was out, which made Cozy furious; the number had originally been Stuff's.
473.ch: Cab Calloway's band, features and small groups
473.q: He would tell him, "Drum number's out." And we'd watch Cozy all during the show, and he'd be sweating and he'd be so mad, he'd be sweating and sweating, it rolled off of him. And he didn't cool off for the whole hour, and when he come off, and if the curtain closed, he'd say, "Hey, Cab, come here.…

473.t: Telling Cab off over the high note in "I Can't Give You Anything but Love"
473.s: Jealous bandmates grumbled about Cab's featuring Jonah in a singing number; at a Sherman Hotel rehearsal he saved his lip, Cab insisted he play the high note, and Jones muttered a rude reply that Cab overheard.
473.ch: Cab Calloway's band, features and small groups
473.q: Oh, a few guys did. Of course the original guys didn't say much, guys like me. I guess we expected it, you know. I had to talk to him once and I was sorry I did, because it didn't call for that, you know.

473.t: Illinois Jacquet, "Rhythm Cocktail" and Cab keeping control of soloists
473.s: Jacquet demanded a feature and got "Rhythm Cocktail", a version of "Flying Home"; Jones thinks Cab limited solos so he would not lose control as Duke did.
473.ch: Cab Calloway's band, features and small groups
473.q: And here comes Illinois Jacquet. Here comes the wrecking crew starting in now. He's had gentlemen in the band all the time had been pretty good. Now they get Illinois Jacquet. Well, "Flying Home" Illinois - this thing. Everybody owns it. Hamp says it's his. Arnett Cobb says it's his, Illinois says…

473.t: Shad Collins's silences and Cab's derby knock
473.s: Jones always asked for Shad Collins despite his sulky silence all day until the fourth show; Cab's habit of knocking his derby when someone made a mistake made the band nervous.
473.ch: Cab Calloway's band, features and small groups
473.q: I think on one number there. They weren't featured too much, but I think they had one number. But there was an argument down there too, because they would come to me and tell me, because Cab a lot of the time would come to me and say, "We're going to enlarge the band again. So who do you think,"…

473.t: Joining Cab Calloway in Pittsburgh and Cab's three rules
473.s: He joined Cab at Pittsburgh's Stanley Theater on February 21; Dizzy warned the show was fixed for a year, and Cab asked only that he be on time, play the music and wear the uniforms; he stayed eleven years.
473.q: So then I went on out and joined -- February 21st, I remember, I joined Cab, you know, and he was playing the Stanley Theater out there in Pittsburgh. So I walked in and

473.t: Final Cab band: Birdland and the Uruguay carnival tour
473.s: His last engagement was at Birdland; Cab had enlarged the band again for a carnival tour of Uruguay with Doc Cheatham, Shad Collins, Ike Quebec and Sam Taylor, Hilton Jefferson.
473.ch: Cab Calloway's band, features and small groups
473.q: I left Cab -- my last engagement was at Birdland, around about February or March or something like that, that was the last. Because we had reorganized again and made the -- after having the four pieces we had raised it back up to a big band again, which we went down to Uruguay, Montevideo, and…

1.t: Cab Calloway always paid and musicians sent money home
1.s: Milt says Cab never missed a payment and would advance money so musicians could provide for their families.
1.ch: Danny's rise through New York bands to Cab Calloway
1.q: Yeah, it the thing with security there, man.

1.t: Why Cab Calloway's band was the height of the band business
1.s: Danny says Cab paid better, bought uniforms, traveled first class, and Mr. Wright was like a daddy to the band.
1.ch: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
1.q: Well, ...(?)... decided to come back to New Orleans. But like, I'd been with Cab Calloway, and this was the height you could go in the band business, with the big Swing bands... It was the height, the most highly respected

1.t: Cab refuses to let Herman Stark fire the band
1.s: When Herman Stark demanded they be fired, Cab said nobody fires his band but him.
1.ch: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
1.q: No. Don't mess with his band.

1.t: Pullman berths, Cozy Cole's practice pad and dressing-room moves
1.s: Barker describes first-class Pullman berths by seniority and the theatre dressing rooms, moving upstairs to escape Cozy Cole's drum practice.
1.q: I joined Cab’s band, and I’m playing. The dressing room. They traveled my first class by train, and I’m in a train on a Pullman. You travel by Pullman. You sleep on . . . Nobody wants to go in the upper berth, because you got to climb up there to get in there. All the old timers, they got the main…

70.t: Calloway traveled first class: uniforms, shoes and discipline
70.s: Calloway paid for five sets of uniforms and shoes and required cleanliness; the gentlemanly discipline made weaker new men straighten up.
70.q: It was, but that was a beautiful way -- That band traveled, I think, first class. I think it was one of the first bands that traveled first class.

70.t: Calloway as a disciplined leader and Buster Harding's farm system
70.s: A band is no greater than its leader; Calloway demanded discipline and kept replacements ready through arranger Buster Harding.
70.q: Well, you see, Calloway himself -- you know, I've always said, and it's been said a lot of times, a band is no greater than its leader, --

70.t: Calloway as entertainer who could count the house
70.s: Jackson and Hinton credit Calloway's entertaining gift; he could feel a crowd and tell within ten how many were in the house.
70.q: And you know something funny, too? I hate to bring this up. But he could come out on that stage and be hidekoing and shaking his hand down at everything and come on stage and tell you just how many people was in that show.

400.t: Cab Calloway pays for Hinton's first child
400.s: Calloway tells Hinton to have the baby on him and covers the costs; Hinton praises him as a man and says too little has been written about him.
400.q: Oh, that’s right, well I says, “Cab my wife is pregnant.” He say, “Yeah, mine too.” He say, “Have this one on me.” So the baby was born, you know, Charlotte was born, and three months later we’re in California and I’m trying to make a two o’clock feed and make the gig that night and Mona’s half…

400.t: Cab as disciplinarian: punctuality, uniforms, payday and Christmas
400.s: Cab insisted on punctuality and paid every dime; he bought uniforms and sent the men home with $100 each Christmas.
400.ch: Cab Calloway's band: road, arrangers and shows
400.q: He was a great disciplinarian. He insisted on time… everybody be on time and of course he said, “I‟ve got to be here. You‟d better be here”. He always had the same… lay dead „til Thursday because Thursday was when he paid off so you just keep cool until Thursday. I never… I don‟t know of anybody…

250.t: The showman bandleader seen in Pensacola
250.s: A jumping bandleader and trumpeter seen on a one-night stop in Pensacola, compared to Cab Calloway.
250.q: You were talking about the little guy. Who was that? I don't know who he was. I really don't know. But I know when he shook it and blew. That was over in Pensacola, Florida when they passed through for one night. And boy the little guy leading their band. If the band would make a scream at the end…

17.t: Cab Calloway as bandleader: entertainer and disciplinarian
17.ch: Dancers, Newton, Chu Berry and the Cab Calloway band
17.q: Cab, well, Cab mostly was an entertainer. And he studied music. I think he studied saxophone with Walter, Foots and some of them, but I guess a man the caliber that Cab was, I mean, couldn't devote too much time to studying music at that part of the game, you know, he was a big top man now you…

381.t: Cab Calloway as the greatest education: discipline and sending money home
381.s: Coming from Lucky's wild band, he watched Cab's veterans wire money home first, and Cab took him aside about his family.
381.q: The greatest education -- I must admit that. Cab Calloway, I will always feel obligated, in a way, to him, because when I joined his band, I had just left Lucky's band which was a wild band, I mean, when I say, 'wild', guys were not oriented as far as being family men, and a lot of them in the band…

124.s: The band was well drilled but Cab was a showman, so McRae told the men he came from the big tent.
124.ch: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
124.q: He was more of a showman and the band didn't have -- really too much to do. And the funny thing, when he turned us loose on an instrumental, you know, it was just like, what's happening here, ain't nothing. You know, like, it's just one of them -- it's always in the (inaudible) Cab Calloway…

7.t: Bawling out Cab during the Bill Robinson show
7.s: While conducting the Cotton Club show, Thomas rebukes a nervous Cab for heckling, later apologizes, and explains Cab picked up bawling out from Rudy Vallee.
7.q: I think it was of Bill's (?)s. Because that's the time when I was the conductor. I didn't have to be in the band, so I was just conducting the band. And Cab got off the wall. He just was nervous about who was going

78.t: Backing Cab Calloway: Minnie the Moocher and conducting by ear
78.s: Horace only backed Calloway when he played where Horace was house band. Cab was no musician but caught arrangements after a couple of rehearsals with help from pianist Benny Payne.
78.ch: Portraits from Hemphill to Getz, and the bebop question
78.q: Yes, he was on the bill. This is when he did It Ain't Necessarily So and, of course, Minnie the Moocher, that was the theme song of his big band in those days. And I think how that came about, you know, he traveled -- the past few years he's been traveling with the Globetrotters, the famous…

103.s: Jones praises Cab Calloway as a disciplinarian and, he says, the most powerful black man alive, who helped bands travel to Army camps in the war.
103.q: And Fess came into the hotel on Central Avenue — and that's one of the first times in my life — you know, Cab Calloway, people don't know but Cab Calloway would work so much and do so many things off the stage, because Cab Calloway was doing so many civic things that people don't know nothing…
